answers.core: I think there's actually be an add-on somewhere that does something similar to this, but "create a button that triggers a function" is probably a common enough use case for tool script writers that it warrants a single-line annotation.
answers.workaround:
There is actually a hack that approximates the necessary functionality: Export a boolean property with a getter that always returns false and a setter which does nothing but trigger a method call. You get a perpetually empty checkbox that triggers a method when clicked. It's not elegant, but it does work:
```GDScript
@tool
extends Node2D

@export var make_me_bigger : bool:
    get:
        return false
    set(b):
        increase_size()

func increase_size():
    scale *= 2
```

title: Add a @tool_button annotation to create inspector buttons for tool scripts
